bull.b: Teradyne's sustained gross margins near 57–60% reflect pricing power, differentiated capital-equipment products and a high-value installed base. Durable margin structure supports long-term operating profitability, funds R&D and capital allocation, and cushions earnings across semiconductor cycles.

A conservative balance sheet with very low leverage and attractive ROE provides flexibility to invest in product development, sustain buybacks/dividends and absorb cyclicality. This financial strength lowers refinancing risk and supports multi-year strategic initiatives and capital allocation.

Significant revenue concentration from AI/compute and management's large WFE/ATE TAM outlook indicate a structural demand tailwind. Traction with hyperscalers, merchant GPU orders and compute exposure supports durable revenue growth prospects and a credible path to midterm share gains.

bear.b: The business exhibits meaningful cyclicality—material revenue declines in prior years and inconsistent cash conversion (operating cash flow below net income in several years). This variability can strain liquidity planning, compress FCF in downturns and complicate multi-year forecasting.

Ongoing memory-driven margin pressure and sequential gross-margin dips reduce confidence in sustained margin expansion. Because memory and product-mix swings can persist across cycles, they may limit long-term operating leverage until product mix or technology transitions stabilize.

Inventory build to support anticipated sales increases near-term cash requirements and can compress free cash flow if order timing slips. Coupled with long 9–12 month qualification and customer dual-vendor dynamics, this raises durable execution risk and can delay sustainable share gains.
